questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q54
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question:
A group of total 16 piles are arranged in a square grid format. The center-to-center spacing (s) between adjacent piles is 3 m. The diameter (d) and length of embedment of each pile are 1 m and 20 m, respectively. The design capacity of each pile is 1000 kN in the vertical downward direction. The pile group efficiency (ηg) is given by
\[ \eta_g = 1 - \dfrac{\theta}{90} \left[\dfrac{(n-1)m + (m-1)n}{mn} \right] \]
where m and n are number of rows and columns in the plan grid of pile arrangement, and \( \theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{d}{s}\right) \).

The design value of the pile group capacity (in kN) in the vertical downward direction is _________________. (round off to the nearest integer)
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Deep Foundations

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Total number of piles = 16, in a \(4 \times 4\) square grid (\(m = 4\) rows, \(n = 4\) columns)
    • Spacing between piles, \(s = 3 \text{ m}\)
    • Diameter of each pile, \(d = 1 \text{ m}\)
    • Capacity of single pile, \(Q_u = 1000 \text{ kN}\)
    • Group efficiency formula: Converse-Labarre equation
  • Aim: Calculate the pile group capacity (\(Q_{ug}\)) in kN.

3. Core Concepts:

Pile Group Efficiency (\(\eta_g\)): Due to overlapping stress zones of closely spaced friction piles, group capacity is often less than the sum of individual capacities.

Converse-Labarre Formula: \[ \eta_g = 1 - \dfrac{\theta}{90} \left[\dfrac{(n-1)m + (m-1)n}{mn}\right] \] where \(\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{d}{s}\right)\) in degrees.

Pile Group Capacity: \(Q_{ug} = \eta_g \times N \times Q_u\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate angle \(\theta\).
  2. Substitute into the efficiency formula.
  3. Compute the group capacity.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate \(\theta\):
    \[\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) = 18.4349^\circ \]
  2. Bracket Term:
    \[\dfrac{(n-1)m + (m-1)n}{mn} = \dfrac{(3)(4) + (3)(4)}{16} = \dfrac{12 + 12}{16} = 1.5 \]
  3. Group Efficiency:
    \[\eta_g = 1 - \dfrac{18.4349}{90} \times 1.5 = 1 - 0.20483 \times 1.5 = 1 - 0.30725 = 0.69275 \]
  4. Group Capacity:
    \[Q_{ug} = 0.69275 \times 16 \times 1000 = 11{,}084 \text{ kN} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 11084 kN | Accepted key range: 11000 to 11200

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q55
questions.subject: Geotechnical Engineering (Soil)
questions.question: A saturated compressible clay layer of thickness h is sandwiched between two sand layers, as shown in the figure. Initially, the total vertical stress and pore water pressure at point P, which is located at the mid-depth of the clay layer, were 150 kPa and 25 kPa, respectively. Construction of a building caused an additional total vertical stress of 100 kPa at P. When the vertical effective stress at P is 175 kPa, the percentage of consolidation in the clay layer at P is _________. (in integer)
questions.explanation:
Geotechnical Engineering | Soil Mechanics / Consolidation

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Point P at mid-depth of a clay layer (double drainage)
    • Initial total vertical stress, \(\sigma_0 = 150 \text{ kPa}\)
    • Initial pore water pressure, \(u_0 = 25 \text{ kPa}\)
    • Additional total stress from building, \(\Delta\sigma = 100 \text{ kPa}\)
    • Current vertical effective stress, \(\sigma'_t = 175 \text{ kPa}\)
  • Aim: Find the percentage of consolidation (\(U_z\)) at point P.

3. Core Concepts:

Principle of Effective Stress: \(\sigma = \sigma' + u\)

Consolidation Phenomenon: Upon loading saturated clay, the initial increase in total stress (\(\Delta\sigma\)) is entirely borne by pore water (\(\Delta u_i = \Delta\sigma\)). As water escapes, excess pore pressure dissipates and transfers to the soil skeleton.

Degree of Consolidation: \[U_z = \dfrac{\sigma'_t - \sigma'_0}{\sigma'_f - \sigma'_0} \times 100\% \]

4. Solution Method:

Method 1 (Effective Stress): Compute \(\sigma'_0\) and \(\sigma'_f\), then interpolate using \(\sigma'_t\).
Method 2 (Pore Pressure): Determine initial and current excess pore pressure to calculate \(U_z\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Initial Effective Stress (\(\sigma'_0\)):
    \[\sigma'_0 = 150 - 25 = 125 \text{ kPa} \]
  2. Ultimate Effective Stress (\(\sigma'_f\)):
    \[\sigma'_f = \sigma'_0 + \Delta\sigma = 125 + 100 = 225 \text{ kPa} \]
  3. Degree of Consolidation:
    \[U_z = \dfrac{175 - 125}{225 - 125} \times 100\% = \dfrac{50}{100} \times 100\% = 50\% \]

Validation via Pore Pressure Method:
Current total stress: \(\sigma_t = 150 + 100 = 250 \text{ kPa}\)
Current pore pressure: \(u_t = 250 - 175 = 75 \text{ kPa}\)
Current excess pore pressure: \(\Delta u_t = 75 - 25 = 50 \text{ kPa}\)
Initial excess pore pressure: \(\Delta u_i = 100 \text{ kPa}\)
\[U_z = \left(1 - \dfrac{50}{100}\right) \times 100\% = 50\% \checkmark \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 50% | Accepted key range: 50 to 50

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q56
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
A hydraulic jump takes place in a 6 m wide rectangular channel at a point where the upstream depth is 0.5 m (just before the jump). If the discharge in the channel is 30 m³/s and the energy loss in the jump is 1.6 m, then the Froude number computed at the end of the jump is ____________. (round off to two decimal places)

(Consider the acceleration due to gravity as 10 m/s².)
questions.explanation:
Fluid Mechanics | Open Channel Flow & Hydraulic Jump

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Channel width, \(B = 6 \text{ m}\) (Rectangular channel)
    • Upstream depth, \(y_1 = 0.5 \text{ m}\)
    • Discharge, \(Q = 30 \text{ m}^3/\text{s}\)
    • Energy loss in the jump, \(\Delta E = 1.6 \text{ m}\)
    • Acceleration due to gravity, \(g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2\)
  • Aim: Calculate the Froude number computed at the end of the jump (\(F_{r2}\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Discharge per unit width (\(q\)): \[q = \dfrac{Q}{B} \]

Energy Loss in a Hydraulic Jump (\(\Delta E\)): \[\Delta E = \dfrac{(y_2 - y_1)^3}{4 y_1 y_2} \] where \(y_2\) is the downstream depth.

Froude Number (\(F_{r}\)): For a rectangular channel, \[F_{r2} = \dfrac{v_2}{\sqrt{g y_2}} = \dfrac{q}{\sqrt{g y_2^3}} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the discharge per unit width (\(q\)).
  2. Use the given energy loss and \(y_1\) to form a cubic equation in terms of \(y_2\).
  3. Solve for \(y_2\) by recognizing the integer roots physically possible.
  4. Calculate \(F_{r2}\) using the derived \(y_2\) and \(q\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate \(q\):
    \[q = \dfrac{30}{6} = 5 \text{ m}^3/\text{s/m} \]
  2. Formulate the Energy Loss Equation:
    \[1.6 = \dfrac{(y_2 - 0.5)^3}{4 \times 0.5 \times y_2} = \dfrac{(y_2 - 0.5)^3}{2 y_2} \]
    \[3.2 y_2 = (y_2 - 0.5)^3 \]
  3. Solve for \(y_2\):
    Let \(x = (y_2 - 0.5) \implies y_2 = x + 0.5\). Substituting:
    \[3.2(x + 0.5) = x^3 \implies x^3 - 3.2x - 1.6 = 0 \]
    By inspection, testing \(x = 2\):
    \[(2)^3 - 3.2(2) - 1.6 = 8 - 6.4 - 1.6 = 0 \checkmark \]
    Thus \(x = 2\) is a valid root, so \(y_2 = 2 + 0.5 = 2.5 \text{ m}\).
  4. Calculate Final Froude Number (\(F_{r2}\)):
    \[F_{r2} = \dfrac{q}{\sqrt{g y_2^3}} = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{10 \times (2.5)^3}} = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{10 \times 15.625}} = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{156.25}} = \dfrac{5}{12.5} = 0.40 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.40 | Accepted key range: 0.20 to 0.41

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q57
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
A pump with an efficiency of 80% is used to draw groundwater from a well for irrigating a flat field of area 108 hectares. The base period and delta for paddy crop on this field are 120 days and 144 cm, respectively. Water application efficiency in the field is 80%. The lowest level of water in the well is 10 m below the ground. The minimum required horse power (h.p.) of the pump is ____________. (round off to two decimal places)

(Consider 1 h.p. = 746 W; unit weight of water = 9810 N/m³)
questions.explanation:
Irrigation Engineering | Water Requirements of Crops

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Pump efficiency, \(\eta_p = 80\% = 0.80\)
    • Field Area, \(A = 108 \text{ hectares} = 108 \times 10^4 \text{ m}^2\)
    • Base period, \(B = 120 \text{ days}\)
    • Delta, \(\Delta = 144 \text{ cm} = 1.44 \text{ m}\)
    • Water application efficiency, \(\eta_a = 80\% = 0.80\)
    • Total head (depth to water), \(H = 10 \text{ m}\)
    • Unit weight of water, \(\gamma_w = 9810 \text{ N/m}^3\)
    • Power conversion, \(1 \text{ h.p.} = 746 \text{ W}\)
  • Aim: Find the minimum required horse power (h.p.) of the pump.

3. Core Concepts:

Total Volume required at Field: \(V_{field} = A \times \Delta\)

Total Volume to be Pumped: \(V_{pump} = \dfrac{V_{field}}{\eta_a}\)

Continuous Discharge Required (\(Q\)): \(Q = \dfrac{V_{pump}}{\text{Base Period in seconds}}\)

Power required by the pump (\(P\)): \[P \text{ (in Watts)} = \dfrac{\gamma_w \times Q \times H}{\eta_p} \]

4. Solution Method:

Calculate the actual volume of water the pump must deliver over the entire base period. Convert this to a continuous flow rate (\(Q\)) in m³/s. Apply the power formula, factoring in the pump's mechanical efficiency, and finally convert Watts to horse power.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Volume of Water:
    \[V_{field} = 108 \times 10^4 \times 1.44 = 1{,}555{,}200 \text{ m}^3 \]
    \[V_{pump} = \dfrac{1{,}555{,}200}{0.80} = 1{,}944{,}000 \text{ m}^3 \]
  2. Calculate Discharge (\(Q\)):
    \[B \text{ (in seconds)} = 120 \times 24 \times 3600 = 10{,}368{,}000 \text{ s} \]
    \[Q = \dfrac{1{,}944{,}000}{10{,}368{,}000} = 0.1875 \text{ m}^3/\text{s} \]
  3. Calculate Required Power:
    \[P = \dfrac{9810 \times 0.1875 \times 10}{0.80} = 22{,}992.1875 \text{ W} \]
    \[P_{hp} = \dfrac{22{,}992.1875}{746} = 30.82 \text{ h.p.} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 30.82 | Accepted key range: 30.00 to 32.00

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q58
questions.subject: Water Resources & Hydraulics
questions.question:
Two discrete spherical particles (P and Q) of equal mass density are independently released in water. Particle P and particle Q have diameters of 0.5 mm and 1.0 mm, respectively. Assume Stokes' law is valid.

The drag force on particle Q will be _________ times the drag force on particle P.
(round off to the nearest integer)
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Fluid Mechanics (Stokes' Law)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension / Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Two discrete spherical particles, P and Q
    • Mass densities are equal: \(\rho_P = \rho_Q = \rho_s\)
    • Diameter of P, \(D_P = 0.5 \text{ mm}\)
    • Diameter of Q, \(D_Q = 1.0 \text{ mm}\)
    • Stokes' law is valid (laminar settling regime)
  • Aim: Ratio of drag force on particle Q to drag force on particle P \(\left(\dfrac{F_{DQ}}{F_{DP}}\right)\).

3. Core Concepts:

Stokes' Drag Force: \(F_D = 3\pi \mu V_t D\)

When a particle is released in a fluid and falls in the Stokes' regime, it reaches a Terminal Velocity (\(V_t\)), where the Drag Force exactly balances the Submerged Weight.

Submerged Weight (\(W_{sub}\)): \[W_{sub} = \dfrac{\pi}{6} D^3 \rho_s g - \dfrac{\pi}{6} D^3 \rho_w g = \dfrac{\pi}{6} D^3 (\rho_s - \rho_w) g \]

At terminal velocity: \(F_D = W_{sub} \propto D^3\).

4. Solution Method:

A common pitfall is to calculate the drag ratio directly from \(F_D \propto D\) without considering that terminal velocity \(V_t\) is itself proportional to \(D^2\).
Since \(F_D = 3\pi \mu V_t D\) and \(V_t \propto D^2\), it follows that \(F_D \propto D^3\).
Simply evaluate the cube of the ratio of their diameters.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Formulate the proportionality:
    Since particles have equal density and fall in the same fluid:
    \[F_D \propto D^3 \implies \dfrac{F_{DQ}}{F_{DP}} = \left(\dfrac{D_Q}{D_P}\right)^3 \]
  2. Calculate the ratio:
    \[\dfrac{F_{DQ}}{F_{DP}} = \left(\dfrac{1.0}{0.5}\right)^3 = (2)^3 = 8 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 8 | Accepted key range: 8 to 8

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q59
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: At a municipal waste handling facility, 30 metric ton mixture of food waste, yard waste, and paper waste was available. The moisture content of this mixture was found to be 10%. The ideal moisture content for composting this mixture is 50%. The amount of water to be added to this mixture to bring its moisture content to the ideal condition is _________ metric ton. (in integer)
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Solid Waste Management

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Initial total mass, \(W_1 = 30 \text{ MT}\) (Metric Tons)
    • Initial moisture content, \(M_1 = 10\% = 0.10\)
    • Ideal (target) moisture content, \(M_2 = 50\% = 0.50\)
  • Aim: Amount of water to be added (\(W_w\)) in MT.

3. Core Concepts:

Mass Conservation: In a composting/drying process where only water is added or removed, the Dry Mass (\(W_d\)) remains constant.

Relationship between Total Mass, Dry Mass, and Moisture Content: \[W_d = W_{total} \times (1 - M) \] where \(M\) is the moisture content expressed as a decimal fraction.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Determine the constant dry mass of the solid waste.
  2. Use the ideal final moisture content and the constant dry mass to find the new total mass (\(W_2\)).
  3. The amount of water added is the difference between the final total mass and the initial total mass.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Dry Solid Mass:
    \[W_d = 30 \times (1 - 0.10) = 30 \times 0.90 = 27 \text{ MT} \]
  2. Calculate Final Total Mass (\(W_2\)):
    Let the new total mass be \(W_2\). The moisture content is 50%, so the dry fraction is \((1 - 0.50) = 0.50\).
    \[W_d = W_2 \times (1 - 0.50) \implies 27 = W_2 \times 0.50 \implies W_2 = \dfrac{27}{0.50} = 54 \text{ MT} \]
  3. Calculate Added Water:
    \[W_w = W_2 - W_1 = 54 - 30 = 24 \text{ MT} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 24 | Accepted key range: 24 to 24

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q60
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question:
A sewage treatment plant receives sewage at a flow rate of 5000 m³/day. The total suspended solids (TSS) concentration in the sewage at the inlet of primary clarifier is 200 mg/L. After the primary treatment, the TSS concentration in sewage is reduced by 60 %. The sludge from the primary clarifier contains 2 % solids concentration. Subsequently, the sludge is subjected to gravity thickening process to achieve a solids concentration of 6 %. Assume that the density of sludge, before and after thickening, is 1000 kg/m³.

The daily volume of the thickened sludge (in m³/day) will be_________. (round off to the nearest integer)
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Wastewater Treatment

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Sewage flow rate, \(Q = 5000 \text{ m}^3/\text{day}\)
    • Initial TSS concentration = \(200 \text{ mg/L}\)
    • TSS removal efficiency in primary clarifier = \(60\%\)
    • Initial sludge solids concentration = \(2\%\)
    • Thickened sludge solids concentration = \(6\%\)
    • Density of sludge (before & after thickening), \(\rho = 1000 \text{ kg/m}^3\)
  • Aim: Find the daily volume of the thickened sludge in m³/day.

3. Core Concepts:

Mass of Solids Extracted (\(M_s\)): \[M_s = Q \times \text{Initial TSS} \times \text{Removal Efficiency} \]

Mass-Volume Relationship for Sludge: \[V_{sludge} = \dfrac{M_s}{\rho_{sludge} \times \text{Solids Fraction}} \]

Note: The solid mass \(M_s\) remains constant during the gravity thickening process.

4. Solution Method:

Calculate the daily mass of dry suspended solids removed by the primary clarifier. Use this constant solid mass, along with the given thickened sludge solids fraction and density, to determine the final sludge volume.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Convert Flow Rate to Liters/day:
    \[Q = 5000 \text{ m}^3/\text{day} = 5 \times 10^6 \text{ L/day} \]
  2. Calculate Mass of Removed TSS (\(M_s\)):
    \[\text{Removed TSS Concentration} = 200 \times 0.60 = 120 \text{ mg/L} \]
    \[M_s = (5 \times 10^6 \text{ L/day}) \times 120 \text{ mg/L} = 600 \times 10^6 \text{ mg/day} = 600 \text{ kg/day} \]
  3. Calculate Volume of Thickened Sludge:
    The thickened sludge has a \(6\%\) solid concentration (fraction = \(0.06\)).
    \[V_{thickened} = \dfrac{M_s}{\rho \times \text{Solids Fraction}} = \dfrac{600 \text{ kg/day}}{1000 \text{ kg/m}^3 \times 0.06} = \dfrac{600}{60} = 10 \text{ m}^3/\text{day} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 10 | Accepted key range: 10 to 10

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q61
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question:
A sample of air analyzed at 25 °C and 1 atm pressure is reported to contain 0.04 ppm of SO₂. Atomic mass of S = 32, O = 16.

The equivalent SO₂ concentration (in µg/m³) will be ____________. (round off to the nearest integer)
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Air Pollution

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Temperature, \(T = 25^\circ\text{C} = 298.15 \text{ K}\)
    • Pressure, \(P = 1 \text{ atm}\)
    • Volumetric concentration of SO₂, \(C_{ppm} = 0.04 \text{ ppm} = 0.04 \text{ mL/m}^3\)
    • Molecular Weight of SO₂, \(M = 32 + (2 \times 16) = 64 \text{ g/mol}\)
  • Aim: Equivalent SO₂ concentration in \(\mu\text{g/m}^3\).

3. Core Concepts:

Ideal Gas Law: Determines the volume occupied by one mole of gas (\(V_m\)) at given conditions. \[V_m = \dfrac{R T}{P} \] where Universal Gas Constant, \(R = 0.08205 \text{ L}\cdot\text{atm/(mol}\cdot\text{K)}\)

Conversion Formula: \[C \,(\mu\text{g/m}^3) = \dfrac{C \,(\text{ppm}) \times M \,(\text{g/mol}) \times 10^3}{V_m \,(\text{L/mol})} \] (Since \(1 \text{ ppm} = 1 \text{ mL/m}^3\) and \(1 \text{ mole} = M \text{ g} = M \times 10^6 \, \mu\text{g}\).)

4. Solution Method:

Calculate the molar volume of an ideal gas at \(25^\circ\text{C}\) and \(1 \text{ atm}\). Then apply the standard conversion formula to shift from parts per million (volumetric) to \(\mu\text{g/m}^3\) (mass-based).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Molar Volume (\(V_m\)):
    \[V_m = \dfrac{0.08205 \times 298.15}{1} = 24.463 \text{ L/mol} \]
  2. Convert ppm to \(\mu\text{g/m}^3\):
    \[C \,(\mu\text{g/m}^3) = \dfrac{0.04 \times 64 \times 1000}{24.463} = \dfrac{2560}{24.463} = 104.647 \, \mu\text{g/m}^3 \]
    Rounding off to the nearest integer gives 105.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 105 | Accepted key range: 102 to 108

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q62
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question: A parabolic vertical crest curve connects two road segments with grades +1.0% and –2.0%. If a 200 m stopping sight distance is needed for a driver at a height of 1.2 m to avoid an obstacle of height 0.15 m, then the minimum curve length should be ______ m. (round off to the nearest integer)
questions.explanation:
Transportation Engineering | Highway Geometric Design

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Ascending grade, \(n_1 = +1.0\% = +0.01\)
    • Descending grade, \(n_2 = -2.0\% = -0.02\)
    • Stopping Sight Distance (SSD), \(S = 200 \text{ m}\)
    • Height of driver's eye, \(H = 1.2 \text{ m}\)
    • Height of obstacle, \(h = 0.15 \text{ m}\)
  • Aim: Minimum length of the parabolic vertical crest curve (\(L_c\)).

3. Core Concepts:

Deviation Angle (\(N\)): \(N = |n_1 - n_2|\)

Length of Crest Curve (\(L\)) Formulas (as per IRC):

  • Case 1 (Assuming \(L > S\)): \[L = \dfrac{N S^2}{(\sqrt{2H} + \sqrt{2h})^2} \]
  • Case 2 (Assuming \(L < S\)): \[L = 2S - \dfrac{(\sqrt{2H} + \sqrt{2h})^2}{N} \]

4. Solution Method:

First, calculate the deviation angle \(N\). Next, assume \(L > S\) and compute \(L\). If the calculated length is indeed greater than \(S\), the assumption is correct. Evaluate the denominator properly to avoid rounding errors.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Deviation Angle (\(N\)):
    \[N = |0.01 - (-0.02)| = 0.03 \]
  2. Calculate the Denominator Constant (\(K\)):
    \[K = (\sqrt{2H} + \sqrt{2h})^2 = (\sqrt{2 \times 1.2} + \sqrt{2 \times 0.15})^2 \]
    \[K = (\sqrt{2.4} + \sqrt{0.3})^2 = (1.5492 + 0.5477)^2 = (2.0969)^2 \approx 4.397 \text{ m} \]
    Note: IRC often approximates this constant to 4.4, but exact computation is preferred.
  3. Assume \(L > S\) and Calculate \(L\):
    \[L = \dfrac{N S^2}{K} = \dfrac{0.03 \times (200)^2}{4.397} = \dfrac{0.03 \times 40{,}000}{4.397} = \dfrac{1200}{4.397} = 272.91 \text{ m} \]
  4. Check Assumption:
    Since \(272.91 \text{ m} > 200 \text{ m}\), our initial assumption (\(L > S\)) is correct.
    Rounding off to the nearest integer gives 273.
    Even if using IRC's approximation \(K = 4.4\): \(L = 1200/4.4 = 272.72 \text{ m}\), rounded to 273.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 273 | Accepted key range: 270 to 275

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q63
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question:
Assuming that traffic on a highway obeys the Greenshields model, the speed of a shockwave between two traffic streams (P) and (Q) as shown in the schematic is ______ kmph. (in integer)

Direction of traffic
→
(P)
Flow = 1200 vehicles/hour
Speed = 60 kmph		(Q)
Flow = 1800 vehicles/hour
Speed = 30 kmph
questions.explanation:
Transportation Engineering | Traffic Engineering

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Traffic obeys the Greenshields model.
    • Stream P: Flow \(q_P = 1200 \text{ veh/hour}\), Speed \(v_P = 60 \text{ kmph}\)
    • Stream Q: Flow \(q_Q = 1800 \text{ veh/hour}\), Speed \(v_Q = 30 \text{ kmph}\)
  • Aim: The speed of the shockwave between the two streams in kmph.

3. Core Concepts:

Fundamental Traffic Equation: \(q = k \times v\), where \(q\) is flow, \(k\) is density, and \(v\) is space-mean speed.

Shockwave Speed (\(U_w\)): When traffic states transition from one state to another, the boundary separating these two states moves at a speed: \[U_w = \dfrac{\Delta q}{\Delta k} = \dfrac{q_Q - q_P}{k_Q - k_P} \]

4. Solution Method:

Using the fundamental equation, compute the density for stream P (\(k_P\)) and stream Q (\(k_Q\)). Substitute the flow and density values into the shockwave velocity formula to find the magnitude and direction (sign) of the shockwave.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Densities for Streams P and Q:
    \[k_P = \dfrac{q_P}{v_P} = \dfrac{1200}{60} = 20 \text{ veh/km} \]
    \[k_Q = \dfrac{q_Q}{v_Q} = \dfrac{1800}{30} = 60 \text{ veh/km} \]
  2. Calculate Shockwave Speed (\(U_w\)):
    \[U_w = \dfrac{q_Q - q_P}{k_Q - k_P} = \dfrac{1800 - 1200}{60 - 20} = \dfrac{600}{40} = 15 \text{ kmph} \]
    The positive sign indicates the shockwave propagates in the direction of traffic flow.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 15 | Accepted key range: 15 to 15

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q64
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question:
It is given that an aggregate mix has 260 grams of coarse aggregates and 240 grams of fine aggregates. The specific gravities of the coarse and fine aggregates are 2.6 and 2.4, respectively. The bulk specific gravity of the mix is 2.3.

The percentage air voids in the mix is ____________. (round off to the nearest integer)
questions.explanation:
Highway Engineering | Pavement Materials

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Mass of coarse aggregates, \(W_c = 260 \text{ g}\)
    • Mass of fine aggregates, \(W_f = 240 \text{ g}\)
    • Specific gravity of coarse aggregates, \(G_c = 2.6\)
    • Specific gravity of fine aggregates, \(G_f = 2.4\)
    • Bulk specific gravity of the mix, \(G_b = 2.3\)
  • Aim: Calculate the percentage of air voids in the aggregate mix.

3. Core Concepts:

Theoretical Maximum Specific Gravity (\(G_t\)): Also known as the maximum theoretical density (assuming zero air voids), it is the weighted harmonic mean of the specific gravities of the individual components. \[G_t = \dfrac{W_{total}}{V_{solid}} = \dfrac{W_c + W_f}{\dfrac{W_c}{G_c} + \dfrac{W_f}{G_f}} \]

Percentage of Air Voids (\(V_a\)): The air voids are calculated by comparing the actual bulk specific gravity of the mix (\(G_b\)) to its theoretical maximum specific gravity (\(G_t\)). \[V_a = \left(1 - \dfrac{G_b}{G_t}\right) \times 100 \]

4. Solution Method:

First, use the mass and specific gravity of each aggregate fraction to find the theoretical maximum specific gravity (\(G_t\)) of the combined mix. Then, apply the air void formula using the given bulk specific gravity (\(G_b\)).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Theoretical Maximum Specific Gravity (\(G_t\)):
    \[G_t = \dfrac{260 + 240}{\dfrac{260}{2.6} + \dfrac{240}{2.4}} = \dfrac{500}{100 + 100} = \dfrac{500}{200} = 2.5 \]
  2. Calculate Percentage of Air Voids (\(V_a\)):
    \[V_a = \left(1 - \dfrac{2.3}{2.5}\right) \times 100 = (1 - 0.92) \times 100 = 0.08 \times 100 = 8\% \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 8 | Accepted key range: 8 to 8

questions.title: GATE CE 2022 Set 2 | CE Q65
questions.subject: Transportation Engineering
questions.question:
The lane configuration with lane volumes in vehicles per hour of a four-arm signalized intersection is shown in the figure. There are only two phases: the first phase is for the East-West and the West-East through movements, and the second phase is for the North-South and the South-North through movements. There are no turning movements. Assume that the saturation flow is 1800 vehicles per hour per lane for each lane and the total lost time for the first and the second phases together is 9 seconds.



The optimum cycle length (in seconds), as per the Webster's method, is ____________. (round off to the nearest integer)
questions.explanation:
Transportation Engineering | Traffic Engineering (Signal Design)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Phase 1: East-West and West-East through movements
      • West-East lane volumes: \(504 \text{ veh/hr}\) and \(504 \text{ veh/hr}\)
      • East-West lane volumes: \(440 \text{ veh/hr}\) and \(460 \text{ veh/hr}\)
    • Phase 2: North-South and South-North through movements
      • North-South lane volume: \(396 \text{ veh/hr}\)
      • South-North lane volume: \(360 \text{ veh/hr}\)
    • Saturation flow per lane, \(s = 1800 \text{ veh/hr/lane}\)
    • Total lost time, \(L = 9 \text{ seconds}\)
  • Aim: Determine the optimum cycle length in seconds using Webster's method.

3. Core Concepts:

Critical Lane Volume (\(q_c\)): For any given phase, the critical lane is the one carrying the maximum traffic volume, as this lane dictates the required green time for the entire phase. \[q_{ci} = \max(q_{\text{lane 1}},\, q_{\text{lane 2}},\, \dots \text{ for Phase } i) \]

Flow Ratio (\(y_i\)): Ratio of critical lane volume to its saturation flow. \[y_i = \dfrac{q_{ci}}{s} \]

Total Flow Ratio (\(Y\)): Sum of critical flow ratios of all phases. \[Y = \sum y_i = y_1 + y_2 \]

Webster's Optimum Cycle Length (\(C_o\)): \[C_o = \dfrac{1.5L + 5}{1 - Y} \] where \(L\) is the total lost time per cycle.

4. Solution Method:

Evaluate the lane volumes provided in the intersection schematic phase by phase. Since saturation flow (\(s\)) is uniform across all lanes, simply identify the highest volume lane in Phase 1 to calculate \(y_1\), and the highest volume lane in Phase 2 to calculate \(y_2\). Sum these to get \(Y\), and compute \(C_o\) using Webster's formula.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Determine Critical Flow Ratio for Phase 1 (\(y_1\)):
    Phase 1 includes all East-West and West-East lanes.
    \[q_{c1} = \max(504,\, 504,\, 440,\, 460) = 504 \text{ veh/hr} \]
    \[y_1 = \dfrac{504}{1800} = 0.28 \]
  2. Determine Critical Flow Ratio for Phase 2 (\(y_2\)):
    Phase 2 includes the North-South and South-North lanes.
    \[q_{c2} = \max(396,\, 360) = 396 \text{ veh/hr} \]
    \[y_2 = \dfrac{396}{1800} = 0.22 \]
  3. Calculate Total Flow Ratio (\(Y\)):
    \[Y = y_1 + y_2 = 0.28 + 0.22 = 0.50 \]
  4. Calculate Optimum Cycle Length (\(C_o\)):
    \[C_o = \dfrac{1.5 \times 9 + 5}{1 - 0.50} = \dfrac{13.5 + 5}{0.50} = \dfrac{18.5}{0.50} = 37 \text{ seconds} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 37 | Accepted key range: 37 to 37
